stem: Hydrogen iodide, $\text{HI}$, is a colourless gas at room temperature.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Explain why $\text{HI}$ has a higher boiling point than $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HBr}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The bar chart shows the boiling points of $\text{HCl}$, $\text{HBr}$ and $\text{HI}$. The boiling point of $\text{HF}$ is not shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Hydrogen bonds form between $\text{HF}$ molecules.

Draw a bar on the bar chart to predict the boiling point of $\text{HF}$.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The standard enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus}$, of $\text{HI(g)}$ is $+26.5\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Define the term *standard enthalpy change of formation*.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{HI(g)}$ can be formed by reacting $\text{H}_{2}\text{(g)}$ with $\text{I}_{2}\text{(g)}$. The reaction is reversible, and an equilibrium forms quickly at high temperatures.

$$\text{H}_{2}\text{(g)} + \text{I}_{2}\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI(g)}$$
parts.text: Construct an expression for the equilibrium constant, $K_{\text{p}}$, for the reaction of $\text{H}_{2}\text{(g)}$ and $\text{I}_{2}\text{(g)}$ to form $\text{HI(g)}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The equilibrium partial pressures of the gases at $200^{\circ}\text{C}$ are as follows.

$$p_{\text{H}_{2}\text{(g)}} = 895\text{ Pa}$$

$$p_{\text{I}_{2}\text{(g)}} = 895\text{ Pa}$$

$$p_{\text{HI(g)}} = 4800\text{ Pa}$$

Calculate $K_{\text{p}}$ for this reaction.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
State how the value of $K_{\text{p}}$ would change, if at all, if the reaction were carried out at $100^{\circ}\text{C}$ rather than $200^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: $\text{HI}$ reacts with oxygen to form iodine and water.
parts.text: Construct an equation for the reaction of $\text{HI}$ with oxygen.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Explain, with reference to oxidation numbers, why this reaction is a redox reaction.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
$\text{HI(g)}$ can also be formed by the reaction of $\text{I}_{2}\text{(g)}$ with hydrazine, $\text{N}_{2}\text{H}_{4}\text{(g)}$.

$$2\text{I}_{2}\text{(g)} + \text{N}_{2}\text{H}_{4}\text{(g)} \rightarrow 4\text{HI(g)} + \text{N}_{2}\text{(g)}$$

State the change in pressure that would occur when $2\text{ mol }\text{I}_{2}\text{(g)}$ fully reacts with $1\text{ mol }\text{N}_{2}\text{H}_{4}\text{(g)}$ in a sealed container at constant temperature. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.stem:
In the laboratory, $\text{HI(aq)}$ can be formed in a two-step process.

**step 1** $$3\text{I}_{2}\text{(s)} + 2\text{P(s)} \rightarrow 2\text{PI}_{3}\text{(s)}$$

**step 2** $$\text{PI}_{3}\text{(s)} + 3\text{H}_{2}\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{H}_{3}\text{PO}_{3}\text{(aq)} + 3\text{HI(aq)}$$
parts.text: Draw a 'dot-and-cross' diagram of a $\text{PI}_{3}$ molecule.

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction in **step 2**.

parts.label: (f)(iii)
parts.text:
$\text{H}_{3}\text{PO}_{3}\text{(aq)}$ and $\text{HI(aq)}$ are both strong Brønsted-Lowry acids.

Give the meaning of the term *strong Brønsted-Lowry acid*.

parts.label: (f)(iv)
parts.text: Give the formula of the conjugate base of $\text{H}_{3}\text{PO}_{3}$.

parts.label: (g)(i)
parts.stem: $\text{HI(g)}$ reacts with propene, $\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH=CH}_{2}\text{(g)}$ to form a mixture of 1-iodopropane and 2-iodopropane.
parts.text:
Identify which of 1-iodopropane and 2-iodopropane is the major product of this reaction.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (g)(ii)
